title: The River Takes Another Valley

plate.narration: Two valleys run between the glacier ridges. An old path follows one; fresh water fills the other. High on the slope, a chipped stone marker still points along the ridge.

goal.text: Follow the changed river and find a safe way across.

steps.label: Get across to the far path

arrival.narration: Pip Thistledown, a young manticore scout, stops so suddenly that his notebook bumps his nose. Water is roaring through a valley his sketch shows dry. The road toward the glacier ends at the new stream. A yeti worker raises a staff from the high bank. "Stay up there! Help me warn the next traveler, then get us and our tools across." Pip shuts the notebook. "The road has made changes without telling the map."

choices.label: Find out what needs doing

variants.text: Your party chose to lead Pip's traveling page with the road plan. He keeps it open to compare with this changed route.
Pip keeps the uncertain stone count on his traveling page and opens a fresh space for what the valley shows now.

look_again.narration: An old route marker has a fork-shaped chip. That has not changed. Below it, the old melt channel lies dry while water pours between two ridges farther west. A yeti route worker waits above the new flow; a tool bundle sits on the opposite bank. Pip turns his sketch the right way up, then checks it once more. What will you compare to find out what moved?

choices.label: Compare the marker with both ridges
Trace the dry channel from firm ground
Use the traveling road plan to check the changed landmarks

look_again_1.narration: You keep your feet on the upper path while Pip holds his drawing against the horizon. One friend checks the chipped marker; another points out the ridges. You look for the same shapes in the same order before putting a name on the water below.

choices.label: Put the plan into action

look_again_2.narration: You follow the visible bed only along its firm upper edge. Pip watches where it joins the valley ahead. Your party marks the last place water has recently passed without stepping into the new stream or assuming the dry stones will stay dry.

choices.label: Put the plan into action

look_again_1_check.prompt: Compare the marker with both ridges. Choose who leads while the others help.

look_again_2_check.prompt: Trace the dry channel from firm ground. Choose who leads while the others help.

look_again_1_done.narration: The marker and ridges still agree with the drawing. The water has taken another valley between them. Pip puts his finger on the blank space west of the old channel. You have a changed route to investigate, rather than a reason to throw away every familiar landmark.

choices.label: Continue with this result

look_again_1_changed.narration: A curl of snow hides one ridge and your first comparison points the wrong way. You wait for the gust to pass and compare the chipped marker again. The correction leaves the same conclusion: the landmarks agree, but the water between them has changed its course.

choices.label: Continue with this result

look_again_2_done.narration: The marker and ridges still agree with the drawing. The water has taken another valley between them. Pip puts his finger on the blank space west of the old channel. You have a changed route to investigate, rather than a reason to throw away every familiar landmark.

choices.label: Continue with this result

look_again_2_changed.narration: A curl of snow hides one ridge and your first comparison points the wrong way. You wait for the gust to pass and compare the chipped marker again. The correction leaves the same conclusion: the landmarks agree, but the water between them has changed its course.

choices.label: Continue with this result

road_plan.narration: Your party chose to carry the road plan from the stone keepers. Pip opens its measured landmarks beside the changed valley. You already have a way to distinguish a moved route from a missing marker; the worker only needs you to test the new view against it.

choices.label: Compare the new view with our road plan

road_plan_check.prompt: Use your checked road-plan landmarks to compare the new route.

worksite.narration: A yeti route worker meets you on the near bank. Across the changed stream, a second worker waits on a low shelf beside tools and an unlit lantern. A high path leads from that shelf toward the reading rooms. The near worker has two ropes and a carrying board. "One job before you cross: lift the tools high, or prepare her upper handline. We will need the other if the water changes." Pip studies both valleys.

choices.label: Continue

test_flow.narration: The worker drops a small twig into the new stream. From the dry bank, judge where it passes the central rock. The slow pocket can carry a line; no hero will stand in it.

interaction.cue: Mark the twig's passage through the calm pocket.

onSuccess.narration: You mark a calm pocket behind the central rock.

onFailure.narration: Spray hides the twig. The worker tests again with her marked pole from the bank and shows the calm pocket.

onAssisted.narration: You mark a calm pocket behind the central rock.

flow_result.narration: The calm pocket leads to a low shelf crossing. A longer high rock reach avoids it. Neither is a promise that the water will stay here. The workers pass a guide rope across the calm pocket and test it from both banks. The far worker lights her lantern and lifts it to show she can see you, then waits for your plan.

choices.label: Continue

bundle_plan.narration: There is time for one preparation before your party crosses. Lift the tools to a high rack and they will stay dry, but the far worker will still need help finding the upper handline if the water changes. Rig that handline first and she can withdraw herself; her tools will stay low until you can recover them. Which job comes first?

choices.label: Lift the tools high; help the worker later
Rig the worker's upper handline; recover tools later
Have our duskrunner guide the tools onto the high rack
Have our thornguard brace the upper handline

tools_hoist.narration: The far worker puts the tool bundle on the board. Guide her hauling line toward the rack above the wet seam. The rack is broad; its approach is awkward.

interaction.cue: Guide the board toward the high rack.

onSuccess.narration: The board lands on the rack. The tools are above the waterline.

onFailure.narration: A strap catches below the rack. The far worker holds it on the shelf while you prepare the slower lift.

onAssisted.narration: The board lands on the rack. The tools are above the waterline.

tools_hoist_assisted.narration: The far worker puts the tool bundle on the board. Guide her hauling line toward the rack above the wet seam. The rack is broad; its approach is awkward. Your duskrunner keeps the straps clear, giving the board a wider landing.

interaction.cue: Guide the board toward the high rack.

onSuccess.narration: The board lands on the rack. The tools are above the waterline.

onFailure.narration: A strap catches below the rack. The far worker holds it on the shelf while you prepare the slower lift.

onAssisted.narration: The board lands on the rack. The tools are above the waterline.

tools_steps.narration: The far worker takes the board up the checked stone steps. Keep its load level from your line while she raises each end onto the rack.

interaction.cue: Level the tool board before the worker lifts it.

onSuccess.narration: The slow lift puts every tool on the high rack.

onFailure.narration: The slow lift puts every tool on the high rack.

onAssisted.narration: The slow lift puts every tool on the high rack.

tools_tie.narration: Pass the loose end of the retaining line along the near bank. The far worker uses the returned length to secure the rack. Her upper handline still needs preparing later.

interaction.cue: Pass the retaining line along the bank.

onSuccess.narration: The tools are secured high. The far worker still has the low shelf as her working place.

onFailure.narration: The tools are secured high. The far worker still has the low shelf as her working place.

onAssisted.narration: The tools are secured high. The far worker still has the low shelf as her working place.

people_line.narration: From the near bank, support the guide board while the far worker fixes a handline between her low shelf and the high path. The tool bundle waits beside her lantern.

interaction.cue: Steady the board while the worker fixes the upper handline.

onSuccess.narration: The upper handline is fixed. The tools are still on the low shelf.

onFailure.narration: The upper handline is fixed. The tools are still on the low shelf.

onAssisted.narration: The upper handline is fixed. The tools are still on the low shelf.

people_braced.narration: Your thornguard uses a skill called Brace to hold the guide board in place. The far worker can fix her upper handline without the party doing the board-support task. Her tool bundle remains on the low shelf.

choices.label: Continue

people_signal.narration: Wait for the worker to reach the top of her new handline, then raise the lantern to confirm the route. Her return path is ready; the tools will need collecting later.

interaction.cue: Confirm when the worker reaches the high-path interval.

onSuccess.narration: The worker reaches the high path and returns to her watch, with the handline ready behind her.

onFailure.narration: The lantern signal comes early. The worker waits, then points out the checked upper path herself before returning to watch.

onAssisted.narration: The worker reaches the high path and returns to her watch, with the handline ready behind her.

signals.narration: The workers demonstrate their crossing signs: lantern up for wait, staff sideways for stop, a hand toward the path for proceed. Watch their practice pattern, then show it back. Pip tries to hold a pencil and signal at once. The pencil loses.

interaction.cue: Watch the workers' signal pattern, then echo it.

onSuccess.narration: Both workers can distinguish stop, wait and proceed.

onFailure.narration: The workers slow the demonstration and repeat the signs aloud. Nobody starts across until the meanings are shared.

onAssisted.narration: Both workers can distinguish stop, wait and proceed.

camp.narration: The near worker shares warm tea from a flask while everyone rests on the upper bank. Pip draws two river lines and puts his eraser away. The far worker watches from the low shelf. Your preparation is ready, and the party still needs to reach the far path together.

choices.label: Rest, then choose the crossing
Rest while checking both routes

crossing_choice.narration: The low shelf has a guide rope and a calm pocket. The high rock reach takes longer but stays above the low ice. If your chosen route shifts, the workers will help you use the other one. You will play that changed crossing, not repeat the same attempt. Which route will your party try?

choices.label: Cross by the supported low shelf
Cross by the high rock reach

crossing_choice_1_check.narration: Wait for the worker's clear interval before moving along the supported low shelf. Everyone follows the same checked route.

interaction.cue: Take the low-shelf step in the clear interval.

onSuccess.narration: Your party reaches the far path along the supported low shelf.

onFailure.narration: The low shelf shifts. You return to the near bank before taking the high rock reach together.

onAssisted.narration: Your party reaches the far path along the supported low shelf.

crossing_choice_2_check.narration: The worker points out the next checked foothold on the high rock reach. Wait for her clear interval before taking it. The low guide line stays available if this approach shifts.

interaction.cue: Move across the high reach during the worker's clear interval.

onSuccess.narration: Your party reaches the far path by the high rock reach.

onFailure.narration: A foothold shifts before you commit. The worker redirects you to the supported low shelf.

onAssisted.narration: Your party reaches the far path by the high rock reach.

high_recovery.narration: Keep the high guide line steady while your party follows the worker's longer rock route. This is the way the party actually finishes.

interaction.cue: Steady the guide line for the high rock reach.

onSuccess.narration: Your changed plan gets everyone across by the high rock reach.

onFailure.narration: Your changed plan gets everyone across by the high rock reach.

onAssisted.narration: Your changed plan gets everyone across by the high rock reach.

low_recovery.narration: The workers hold the low crossing steady while your party follows the supported shelf. The checked backup replaces the shifted high foothold.

interaction.cue: Keep the guide board level for the low-shelf crossing.

onSuccess.narration: Your changed plan gets everyone across along the supported low shelf.

onFailure.narration: Your changed plan gets everyone across along the supported low shelf.

onAssisted.narration: Your changed plan gets everyone across along the supported low shelf.

crossing_choice_1_done.narration: The chosen route holds and the party reaches the far path together. The workers wait until the last friend is on firm ground before lifting the stop signal. Pip checks every face, then gives the all-clear. Your crossing plan has worked without leaving anyone behind. You finish along the supported low shelf.

choices.label: Continue with this result

crossing_choice_2_done.narration: The chosen route holds and the party reaches the far path together. The workers wait until the last friend is on firm ground before lifting the stop signal. Pip checks every face, then gives the all-clear. Your crossing plan has worked without leaving anyone behind. You finish by the high rock reach.

choices.label: Continue with this result

river_turn.narration: From the far path, you can see both valleys. Water noses into the old bed while the western stream grows quieter. Pip puts down his eraser. "It is changing back." Watch the order of the visible changes before the workers need your help.

choices.label: Continue

return_observation.narration: The worker points to the changing water. Watch the observation pattern for the western stream, old bed and quiet western channel. Remember which changed first.

interaction.cue: Watch the water-change pattern, then echo it.

onSuccess.narration: You keep the whole visible sequence in order.

onFailure.narration: Spray hides the middle change. You keep the before-and-after landmarks and leave that moment blank.

onAssisted.narration: You keep the whole visible sequence in order.

return_water.narration: The old bed is filling. Your party is on the far high path; the workers are ready to withdraw. The job you prepared determines what still needs help below. You can take that job, or let the workers finish it while your party helps move their repair gear afterward.

choices.label: Let the workers finish; help with repair gear
Our tools are high: guide the worker to the upper path
Her handline is ready: recover the low tool bundle
Use our duskrunner to free the low bundle's straps

worker_beacon.narration: The tools are high, but the far worker still needs a clear route off her low watch. Pass the lantern directions along the high path while the other worker readies a line. She follows the lit landmarks to you.

interaction.cue: Pass the upper-path directions to the worker.

onSuccess.narration: The worker follows the lights onto the high path. The tools remain dry on their rack.

onFailure.narration: The worker follows the lights onto the high path. The tools remain dry on their rack.

onAssisted.narration: The worker follows the lights onto the high path. The tools remain dry on their rack.

tool_recover.narration: The far worker uses the upper handline you prepared and joins you. From the high path, guide a hook toward her low bundle's hauling loop.

interaction.cue: Catch the bundle loop from the high path.

onSuccess.narration: The bundle clears the returning water. Its tools are dry.

onFailure.narration: The water reaches the bundle before the hook catches. The worker draws it onto the high step with her spare line. Everyone stays above the channel.

onAssisted.narration: The bundle clears the returning water. Its tools are dry.

tool_recover_assisted.narration: The far worker uses the upper handline you prepared and joins you. From the high path, guide a hook toward her low bundle's hauling loop. Your duskrunner keeps the loose straps clear, widening the catch.

interaction.cue: Catch the bundle loop from the high path.

onSuccess.narration: The bundle clears the returning water. Its tools are dry.

onFailure.narration: The water reaches the bundle before the hook catches. The worker draws it onto the high step with her spare line. Everyone stays above the channel.

onAssisted.narration: The bundle clears the returning water. Its tools are dry.

wet_tools.narration: The recovered tools are wet. Keep the carrying board level while the workers lay the blades out to dry. The repair will take their afternoon; do not report a dry recovery.

interaction.cue: Level the board for the wet tools.

onSuccess.narration: The workers set aside the wet kit for cleaning. It will need care before another shift.

onFailure.narration: The workers set aside the wet kit for cleaning. It will need care before another shift.

onAssisted.narration: The workers set aside the wet kit for cleaning. It will need care before another shift.

workers_takeover.narration: Your party stays on the upper path while the workers finish the low recovery together. Their spare line and a second trip get everyone and the bundle out. They ask you to move the repair gear to the reading-room path.

variants.text: The tools stay dry on the rack while the workers guide the last low watch out.
The low bundle gets wet before the workers draw it in. The kit needs cleaning.

choices.label: Continue

repair_gear.narration: The workers have used their spare line. Pass the replacement cord and drying cloths along the high path to their repair bundle before leaving.

interaction.cue: Pass the repair supplies along the high path.

onSuccess.narration: The repair supplies are ready. The workers take over the crossing watch.

onFailure.narration: The repair supplies are ready. The workers take over the crossing watch.

onAssisted.narration: The repair supplies are ready. The workers take over the crossing watch.

tell_together.narration: The river runs in its older bed again. The western course still glistens. Pip opens the page to record the crossing and return. You can use the landmarks everyone saw. If you caught the whole return sequence, you can also lead a moving-water reconstruction. Which account will you prepare?

choices.label: Rebuild the known events around fixed landmarks
Use the complete return sequence we watched

record_landmarks.narration: Share the known events without filling the spray-hidden moments. The changed stream was already there when you arrived; your crossing came before it returned to its older bed.

interaction.cue: Arrange the events everyone can place.
clues: The water was already in the dry valley when the party arrived.
The party reached the far path before the river returned.
The river back in its old bed is the final event.

onSuccess.narration: Pip records both river lines and the known order. Any hidden moment stays blank.

onFailure.narration: The workers place the crossing between the two observed river courses. Pip records the corrected order, leaving the hidden moments blank.

onAssisted.narration: Pip records both river lines and the known order. Any hidden moment stays blank.

record_return.narration: Your party watched the complete return. Give the workers the sequence while each of you points out a checked part of the view. Nobody needs to invent why it happened.

interaction.cue: Contribute a checked observation to the account.

options.label: Show where the western stream fell
options.reaction: The worker marks the falling western stream.

options.label: Show where the old bed filled
options.reaction: Pip marks the returning water beside the old channel.

options.label: Show the quiet western course
options.reaction: The wet western line stays on the page for comparison.

onSuccess.narration: The account includes the complete observed return as well as the two course outlines.

onFailure.narration: The account includes the complete observed return as well as the two course outlines.

onAssisted.narration: The account includes the complete observed return as well as the two course outlines.

last_check.narration: Pip pretends to be the next traveler. He stops when your party points out the upper warning. Choose a useful instruction to leave with the lantern. The workers are checking whether the instructions are clear.

interaction.cue: Leave a useful warning for the next traveler.

options.label: Show the upper stopping place
options.reaction: Pip stops at the lantern, well above the old bed.

options.label: Point out both river channels
options.reaction: The worker checks both channels before offering a route.

options.label: Show where to find the route worker
options.reaction: The next traveler has someone to ask when the view changes.

onSuccess.narration: The workers can maintain the upper warning after your party leaves.

onFailure.narration: The workers can maintain the upper warning after your party leaves.

onAssisted.narration: The workers can maintain the upper warning after your party leaves.

rest.narration: The river runs in its older bed again. A wet ribbon in the western valley shows where it briefly went instead. Everyone is across, and the workers keep their lantern on the upper path. Pip closes the sketch with both river lines and the order of the change recorded. "An elder at the reading room has seen something like this in memory ice," says the worker. "Bring your account. She will want to compare it." You can follow the upper path to her or return by the upper road.

variants.text: The high-rack preparation kept the tools dry. The worker's late withdrawal was the job left to finish.
The early upper handline let the worker withdraw herself. The low tool bundle was the job left to finish.
The kit is dry and ready for its next shift.
The workers must clean and dry the wet kit before their next shift.
The complete watched return sequence goes with the two river outlines.
The page preserves the checked landmarks and known order, without inventing the missing detail.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.Pip Thistledown: Manticore scout. Eager but learns to separate observation from guess; never knows an unseen event.
npcVoices.Yeti keepers: Slow, enormous and gentle. Deliberate before answering. Offer a safe method and leave unknown history unknown.
